propositions: Normal compaction, fsck rebuild, and crash recovery each independently derive candidate listing, snapshot detection, snapshot envelope construction, and retired file restoration, causing code duplication across compact_txn.py, compact_rebuild.py, and compact_recovery.py

Multiple independent implementations of the snapshot envelope builder (compact_txn._build_snapshot_event and compact_rebuild inline copy) construct identical structures with identical keys (source_event_uuids, compacted_at) but as separate code

The retired file rename-back rule and its data-loss guard (ensuring all renames succeed before uncommitted snapshot removal) exist separately in compact_txn, compact_recovery, and rollback paths with duplicated os.rename logic

The commit step skeleton (add -A, diff --cached --quiet, commit --no-verify -m) is duplicated between compact_txn._commit_compaction and compact_rebuild._commit_rebuild with only message and error handling varying
The two-arm needs-folding decision rule appears in both compact._scan_snapshot_state and compact_trigger.ticket_needs_folding, including the identical -SNAPSHOT.json probe

A rebuild's candidate scan accepts non-.json files and includes them in source_event_uuids and retired renames, while normal compaction and crash recovery require .json suffix, creating behavioral divergence
